title: The Stag at the Pool

full_text:
A stag came to a crystal pool to drink. Seeing his reflection in the calm water, he admired his magnificent, branching antlers with boundless pride, but felt deep shame at his slender, spindle legs.

"What a tragic contrast!" sighed the stag. "My majestic crown rivals a monarch's diadem, while my wretched legs are thin and weak."

Just then, the baying of hunting hounds and the shouts of hunters echoed through the woods. The stag sprang forward: his swift, slender legs carried him across the open plain like the wind, leaving the hounds far behind.

Entering the dense forest, his branching antlers caught tightly in the hanging branches of an oak. The hounds swarmed upon him. In his dying breath, the stag wept: "How blind I was! The legs I despised would have saved me, while the antlers I foolishly prized have brought my destruction!"
moral: We often despise the useful things that save us, and praise the ornamental vanity that brings ruin.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
